==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*(s)teg-|id2=cover}}
Attested in English since 1530, from {{der|en|la|prōtēctus||covered, protected}}, past participle of {{m|la|prōtegō|prōtegō, prōtegere|to cover the front, protect}} from {{m|la|prō}}, {{affix|la|prō-|t1=before, in front of|tegō|alt2=tegō, tegere|t2=to cover|nocat=1}}, see {{m|en|tegument}}. Largely displaced native Middle English {{m|enm|shelden}}, from Old English {{m|ang|sċildan}} (“to protect,” literally “to shield”).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/pɹəˈtɛkt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-protect.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkt|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To [[keep]] [[safe]]; to [[defend]]; to [[guard]]; to [[prevent]] [[harm]] coming to.
#: {{ux|en|to '''protect''' a child from danger}}
#: {{ux|en|This antivirus package will '''protect''' your computer from hackers.}}
#: {{ux|en|Condoms are designed to '''protect''' against sexually-transmitted diseases.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03
|author=William E. Carter; Merri Sue Carter
|title=The British Longitude Act Reconsidered
|volume=100|issue=2|page=87
|magazine=w:American Scientist
|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/the-british-longitude-act-reconsidered
|passage=But was it responsible governance to pass the Longitude Act without other efforts to '''protect''' British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.}}
# {{lb|en|travel|aviation}} To book a passenger on a later flight if there is a chance they will not be able to board their earlier reserved flight.

====Conjugation====
{{en-conj|old=1}}

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|shield}}
* {{l|en|beshield}}
* See also [[Thesaurus:defend]]
